# Verify with a SAT solver
from pysat.solvers import Glucose3
from itertools import combinations

n = 13
# edge variables
edge_var = {}
v = 1
for i,j in combinations(range(n),2):
    edge_var[(i,j)] = v
    v += 1

def lit(i,j,color):
    # color 0 = red (negative), 1 = blue (positive)
    var = edge_var[(min(i,j),max(i,j))]
    return var if color==1 else -var

solver = Glucose3()
# No red K_4: for every 4-subset, at least one edge must be blue (=1)
for S in combinations(range(n),4):
    clause = [lit(i,j,1) for i,j in combinations(S,2)]
    solver.add_clause(clause)
# No blue K_3: for every 3-subset, at least one edge must be red (=0)
for S in combinations(range(n),3):
    clause = [lit(i,j,0) for i,j in combinations(S,2)]
    solver.add_clause(clause)

print("SAT?", solver.solve())
